messages:
incidentbot: PagerDuty — notification PD-8243 fired for 'router-proxy latency p50 > 200ms' in us-west-2. Triggered by 3 canary failures. Link: https://pd.example/PD-8243

Emma: acked — investigating :mag:

incidentbot: PagerDuty alert acknowledged by Emma (oncall-eng). Auto-escalation in 10m if unresolved.

Raj: seeing spike on proxy CPU around 10:31 UTC, short blip, 3 hosts hit briefly. Collecting logs.

Emma: can you paste the early log tail? Also any client errors?

Raj: logs:
```
2024-03-12T10:31:14Z proxy-4 cpu=92% latency=210ms traces=0
2024-03-12T10:31:15Z proxy-2 cpu=88% latency=220ms traces=0
2024-03-12T10:31:15Z proxy-9 cpu=93% latency=205ms traces=0
```

Sasha: checking SLO dashboards — no 5xxs, only p50 bump for 30s on canaries. No alerts from customers.

Emma: looks transient. Could be synthetic canary churn after deploy to the region earlier today. Any deploys at 10:20?

Raj: no recent deploys in us-west-2. Might be a traffic reroute from infra. I'll run `curl` to the health endpoint across nodes.

Leo: FYI I'll take handoff in 15m, if it still flaps can we keep PD opened? :thumbsup:

incidentbot: PagerDuty automatically resolved PD-8243 after 46s (alerts cleared).

Emma: marking as brief/no-impact. Will keep monitoring for >5m then close.

Sasha: I'll mute synthetic canaries for this region to avoid noisy re-fires while we observe.

Raj: +1 on mute. I'll also run a quick host-level check for thermal throttling.

Emma: thanks — leaving notes in the incident doc. No customer impact reported. Handing off to Leo now.

Leo: taking over — will escalate if it reappears. cc @oncall-next

incidentbot: Note: auto-close timer started. If PD re-triggers within 10m will re-open and notify.

Emma: resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
